note: Literature establishes a broad spectrum from severe infantile hypomyelination to milder childhood-onset spastic ataxia, but studies disagree on whether variant type (truncating vs missense) strictly correlates with severity.

evidence.text: Analysis of a cohort with homozygous NKX6-2 variants and comparison to previously published cases failed to identify clear genotype-phenotype correlations across clinical presentations.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and genetic spectra of NKX6‐2‐related disorder
source.quote: Comparative analysis of our 10 patients and the 15 reported previously did, however, not reveal clear evidence for a genotype-phenotype correlation.

evidence.text: Characterization of NKX6-2 cases demonstrated a broad phenotypic spectrum ranging from severe neonatal onset with global delay to childhood onset with a milder, predominantly motor spastic ataxia phenotype.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: Our data reveal a phenotype spectrum with neonatal onset, global psychomotor delay and worse prognosis at the severe end and a childhood onset with mainly motor phenotype at the milder end.
